name: Heaps
description: Test your knowledge of heap properties, priority queues, and heap-based algorithms.

questions.question: In a max-heap, where is the maximum element located?
questions.explain: By definition, the root of a max-heap contains the largest element in the heap.

questions.question: What is the time complexity of inserting a new element into a binary heap of size n?
questions.explain: Inserting into a heap requires bubbling up the element, which takes logarithmic time relative to the heap size.

questions.question: Which data structure is most commonly implemented using a binary heap?
questions.explain: Heaps are the standard underlying structure for efficient priority queue implementations.

questions.question: What is the time complexity of the 'heapify' operation on an array of size n?
questions.explain: Building a heap from an existing array using the bottom-up heapify method takes linear time.

questions.question: In a complete binary tree representation of a heap, if a node is at index i, what is the index of its left child?
questions.explain: In a zero-indexed array representation, the left child of index i is located at 2i + 1.

questions.question: Which of these is a valid property of a min-heap?
options: The root is the largest element
Every parent is smaller than its children
The tree must be a complete binary tree
The children must be larger than the parent
questions.explain: In a min-heap, the value of each node is less than or equal to the values of its children.

questions.question: What is the time complexity of removing the root element from a heap?
questions.explain: Removing the root requires replacing it with the last element and performing a 'ift-down' operation.

questions.question: How many elements are at the deepest level of a perfect binary heap of height h?
questions.explain: A perfect binary tree of height h has 2^h nodes at its leaf level.

questions.question: Which algorithm uses a heap to sort an array in O(n log n) time?
questions.explain: Heap Sort utilizes the properties of a heap to repeatedly extract the maximum element.

questions.question: What happens to the height of a heap when its size is doubled?
questions.explain: Since a heap is a complete binary tree, its height grows logarithmically with its size.
